### Observed differences

- The dominant difference lies between two groups of five activities. In the earlier window, A21–A25 each appeared in about 85 in 100 traces; in the later window, only in about 18 in 100. A26–A30 moved the opposite way: about 16 in 100 traces earlier, about 82 in 100 later. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, OCC014, OCC015]

- The position of these groups in the flow stayed similar, but their relation to A20 flipped. Earlier, A20 preceded A21–A25 in about 84 in 100 traces and co-occurred with A26–A30 in only about 16 in 100; later, A20 runs without A21–A25 in about 82 in 100 traces and co-occurs with A26–A30 in about 82 in 100, usually before them (about 81 in 100). [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]

- A20's observed outgoing transitions shifted accordingly: earlier about 84% led to A24 and about 15% to A29; later about 82% lead to A29 and about 18% to A24. [DIR006]

- Cohesion within the groups flipped as well: A21–A25 members co-occurred in about 85 in 100 traces earlier and about 18 in 100 later (in about 81 in 100 neither appears), while A26–A30 members co-occurred in about 16 in 100 earlier and about 82 in 100 later. [REL025, REL039, REL058, REL075, REL082, REL093]

- The rising group now feeds the late activities: earlier, A38 and A39 usually appeared without any of A26–A30 (about 84 in 100); later, A26–A30 co-occur with A38/A39 and precede them in about 81 in 100 traces (with A34 they co-occur in about 82 in 100, but the order is mixed: about 47 in 100 before, about 35 interleaved). [REL079, REL080, REL081, REL086, REL091, REL097]

- A04 receded: from about 55 in 100 traces to about 12 in 100, and in the traces where it still occurs it sits around mid-trace (mean relative position about 0.50, more variable) instead of near the end (about 0.94). Earlier, about 95% of A04's observed outgoing transitions went to A39; later, its outgoing transitions spread across many activities. [OCC002, POS001, DIR002]

- The tail into A39 changed accordingly: A38's observed outgoing transitions moved from A04 (about 54%) and A39 (about 45%) earlier to A39 in about 89% later, with A38 directly before A39 (lag 1) in about 90% of cases versus about 45% earlier. [DIR011, LAG010, REL013]

- Secondarily, A02, A06, A08 and A10 became more frequent, from about 2–4 in 100 traces to about 13–18 in 100. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the work executed after A20 changed from the block A21–A25 to the block A26–A30: earlier, A20 was followed by A21–A25 in about 84 in 100 traces and that block ran in about 85 in 100 traces; later, A20 leads into A29 and the block A26–A30 runs in about 82 in 100 traces, preceding A38/A39 in about 81 in 100, while A21–A25 appear in only about 18 in 100 traces. The change is shown directly by the successor change at A20 (A24 to A29) and by the pair-level relation changes around A20, A21–A25, A26–A30, A34, A38 and A39, and it is consistent across all five activities of each group. Chance is unlikely to explain the evidence as a whole: 138 control-flow items qualified against about 1.3 expected if nothing had changed, although many of these items describe the same underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC006, OCC011, DIR006, REL015, REL020, REL080]

The evidence cannot show whether A21–A25 were removed or only became optional (low participation means only that they were rarely observed), nor can it distinguish a single exchange of one block for the other from two independent changes, one removing A21–A25 and one adding A26–A30; a few later-window relations also rest on modest support, for example the A04-related items on about 24 traces. [OCC002, DIR002]

Other differences: A04 nearly vanished from the end of the trace — earlier A38 was followed by A04 in about 54% of its outgoing transitions and A04 led directly to A39 in about 95% of its outgoing, while later A38 proceeds straight to A39 (about 89% of outgoing, directly preceding it in about 90% of cases) and A04, when present, sits mid-trace; A02, A06, A08 and A10 also occur somewhat more often (about 13–18 in 100 traces versus about 2–4 earlier). These may belong to the same overall change but are not required for the main hypothesis. [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, DIR011, LAG010, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]

We have 200 traces before, 200 after. Screening: 260 units tested, 138 items qualified, 1.29 expected by chance without change. That's a massive excess — 138 items vs ~1.3 expected. Now let's understand the behavioural differences.

OCC items:

This is consistent with a replacement of one path/block by another — activities added/removed from traces, not a mere shift in path frequencies. Actually, per the instructions: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows".
